newsitem.title: UK: Smith & Nephew says Dermagraft effective.
newsitem.headline: Smith & Nephew says Dermagraft effective.

text.p: Healthcare group Smith & Nephew Plc said on Tuesday that trials of its skin graft product Dermagraft showed "statistical significance" in treating diabetic foot ulcers compared to standard treatment for the condition.

In a statement the company said trial results of the product were "highly statistically significant", with 60 percent more patients achieving a complete healing of ulcers compared with the current best standard treatment.
Dermagraft is seen as a major new product for Smith & Nephew, and speculation about its prospects has affected the group's share price for the past 12 months.
The company's statement said it would start to market Dermagraft, which effectively builds a living scaffold across wounds to aid the healing process, later this year.
Group director of research and development Alan Suggett said the trials were some of the "most extensive and well-controlled" ever carried out.

"Dermagraft has been shown to heal more wounds and heal them faster than the best standard of care currently available. It represents a real breakthrough in technology for the healing of these very difficult wounds," he said.
The company has already filed a product marketing application for Dermagraft with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and analysts expect a UK launch this summer.
The company, which presented the results at the Symposium on Advanced Woundcare and Medical Research Forum on Wound Repair in New Orleans, said the trial focus was over a 12 week period.
However it said that over 32 weeks, the trial also showed that Dermagraft "continues to stimulate healing even six months after the final application of the product."
It said a high percentage of the 235 patients who took part in the trial "completed the entire 32-week follow-up, demonstrating excellent compliance for a long-term wound healing study."

Last month, analysts at Salomon Brothers said they expected Dermagraft to achieve annual sales of 102 million stg in 1998, rising to a peak of 300 million stg in 2003, and gave the product a valuation of 30 pence per share.
